title: Duplicate WIZNET5K driver/library files in MicroPython tree
body: I noticed that the WIZNET5K files are duplicated in the tree. The copy in lib/wiznet5k appears current and linked to WIZNET development, while drivers/wiznet5k says it was taken from the W5500 EVB ioLibrary in August 2014. It looks like only the STM32 port still relies on the old copy. Should the old files be removed and STM32 changed to use lib/wiznet5k instead? I have no STM32 platform on which to test the change.

symptoms_visible: The tree contains two similar WIZNET5K source sets: a newer copy under lib/wiznet5k and an old 2014 copy under drivers/wiznet5k.
N0.label: N0 duplicate WIZNET5K sources reported

symptoms_visible: A default PYBV11 build produces firmware after changing the source paths, but building with MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K=5500 exposes compile errors, including differing filename case and incompatibilities in the STM32 network wrapper.
N1_x.label: N1_x simple source replacement aftermath

symptoms_visible: Clean PYBV11 builds with MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K=5200 and =5500 now compile and link using lib/wiznet5k.
N2.label: N2 migrated STM32 configuration compiles

symptoms_visible: On a PYBV11 with a W5500 breakout, nic.active(True) raises OSError: 16 and no SPI communication occurs.
The lwIP-enabled build reports that mp_hal_pin_interrupt and the pin-trigger constants are missing.
N3.label: N3 hardware and lwIP testing expose integration failures

symptoms_visible: The earlier migrated build still raises OSError: 16 when activating the W5500; a revised candidate branch is ready for another hardware test.
N4.label: N4 corrected STM32 integration ready for test

symptoms_visible: On the PYBV11 with the W5500 breakout, the revised branch activates the interface and communicates over the network without OSError: 16.
With the interrupt pin and 20 MHz SPI, measured ping times are about 0.75 ms from outside and 1.3 ms from inside.
N5.label: N5 candidate verified on STM32 hardware

symptoms_visible: The consolidated WIZNET5K implementation builds for STM32 and operates on the tested PYBV11 and W5500 hardware without the activation error.
N_terminal.label: terminal migration accepted after hardware verification

solution.intent: Remove drivers/wiznet5k and merely replace the STM32 references with lib/wiznet5k paths.
solution.concrete_example: Delete drivers/wiznet5k, point the STM32 Makefile and network source at lib/wiznet5k, and confirm that the default PYBV11 build completes.

edges.comment: Opening proposal and c0-c8, describing the reporter's working tree and participant1's compile attempt. The initial successful default PYBV11 build had not enabled WIZNET5K; enabling it exposed that a path-only replacement was insufficient.

solution.intent: Complete the compile-time STM32 migration to the newer library by using extmod/network_wiznet5k.c, updating the Makefile's current library paths and filename case, and providing the expected STM32 SPI type name.
solution.concrete_example: Build extmod/network_wiznet5k.c with lib/wiznet5k/Ethernet/W$(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K), add the required library sources and flags, and map machine_spi_type to STM32's machine_hard_spi_type so feature-enabled PYBV11 builds link.
solution.inference_hint: The compile failures show that consolidation requires adapting the STM32 integration to the current shared driver and library layout, rather than only changing directory references.

edges.comment: c9-c23, combining the reporter's and participant1's source changes. The folded user side reports successful clean feature-enabled builds for both W5200 and W5500 after the Makefile, extmod source selection, path case, and SPI type alias were corrected.

question_patterns: Can you load this build on the PYBV11 with the W5500 breakout, call nic.active(True), and report exactly what happens?
Please test the compiled firmware on STM32 hardware and paste any exception raised when the network interface starts.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested it on my PYBV11 with a W5500 breakout. The build succeeds without lwIP, but nic.active(True) raises `OSError: 16`, followed by `MPY: enabling IRQs`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It activates normally and can send traffic on the PYBV11; I see no exception.
I get the same OSError: 16 using a different SPI bus and chip-select pin.

question_patterns: When the activation fails, do you observe any SPI transfers to the W5500?
Can you check whether communication with the W5500 starts before the exception?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Every attempt to communicate with the W5500 fails, and no SPI transfer takes place.

question_patterns: Can you also compile the same STM32 configuration with lwIP enabled and paste the compiler errors, if any?
What raw output do you get from a WIZNET5K and lwIP build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With lwIP enabled, extmod/network_wiznet5k.c fails to compile because `mp_hal_pin_interrupt`, `MP_HAL_PIN_TRIGGER_FALL`, and `MP_HAL_PIN_TRIGGER_NONE` are not defined for this port.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The lwIP-enabled build compiles cleanly and the interrupt pin works, but DHCP never obtains an address.

edges.comment: c19-c28. Hardware and lwIP evidence comes from participant1's PYBV11/W5500 setup and is folded into the simulated user side; the opening reporter explicitly lacked STM32 hardware. These are measurements of the candidate, and the answers retain the raw exception, transfer observation, and compiler names.

solution.intent: Adapt the shared WIZNET driver to STM32's actual SPI object representation and add the STM32 pin-interrupt definitions required by the lwIP mode.
solution.concrete_example: Pass the correct underlying STM32 SPI object to the transfer routine instead of dereferencing the wrapper twice, then implement the pin-interrupt hooks and trigger constants used by the shared WIZNET driver.
solution.inference_hint: participant1 traced the absent transfers to two layers interpreting the SPI value as a wrapper: the constructor had already stored the underlying SPI pointer, while the transfer helper dereferenced it again. The missing lwIP symbols independently require STM32 pin-interrupt support.

edges.comment: c28-c34, based on participant1's diagnosis and candidate branch. This is the final technical correction after the compile-only migration exposed runtime SPI and lwIP interrupt incompatibilities.

question_patterns: Please retest the revised branch on your PYBV11 and W5500 and tell me whether interface activation and network traffic work.
Can you run the same startup script with the updated candidate and report the observed result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The revised branch works on my PYBV11 with the W5500. `nic.active(1)` succeeds, I can configure the interface, and the previous OSError: 16 is gone.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The revised branch still raises OSError: 16 and there is still no SPI traffic.

question_patterns: With the interrupt pin connected, what network behavior or timing do you observe?
Can you test traffic with the interrupt-capable configuration and report the measured ping results?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the interrupt pin and SPI at 20 MHz, ping times are about 0.75 ms from outside and 1.3 ms from inside.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Networking works, with somewhat slower but stable ping times on my setup.

edges.comment: c31-c34. This is pre-landing verification on participant1's real PYBV11 and W5500 hardware, folded into the user side. The answer reports observed activation and ping behavior without turning the measurement into an engineer-side diagnosis.

solution.intent: Land the verified consolidation: remove the obsolete duplicate WIZNET driver, use the current library and shared extmod driver for STM32, and retain the STM32 SPI and interrupt compatibility work proven on hardware.
solution.concrete_example: Replace the STM32 port's old private WIZNET sources with lib/wiznet5k plus extmod/network_wiznet5k.c, including the required Makefile, SPI-object, and interrupt-pin adaptations; accept the change after the PYBV11/W5500 hardware test succeeds.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted resolution is not merely deletion of duplicate files. STM32's dependency on its old private driver concealed integration differences in source layout, driver selection, SPI object representation, and lwIP interrupt support; all had to be adapted and then tested on hardware.

edges.comment: c35 closes the opening reporter's diagnostic chain by stating that the issue was taken care of. The technical content comes from the preceding jointly developed and hardware-verified migration; release and coordination details are not scored.

solution.intent: Perform a complete, compatibility-aware consolidation of STM32 onto the current WIZNET library and shared driver, including compile-time and runtime port adaptations, then verify it on STM32/WIZNET hardware before removal of the old copy is accepted.
solution.concrete_example: Do not only change paths: migrate STM32 to lib/wiznet5k and extmod/network_wiznet5k.c, adapt the Makefile and STM32 SPI/interrupt interfaces expected by that driver, build with WIZNET explicitly enabled, and have someone with a PYBV11/W5500 verify activation and traffic before deleting the old sources.

edges.comment: Shortcut for an agent that proposes the full compatibility-aware migration from the opening report. It skips the real thread's compile and runtime failures but must still request feature-enabled builds and real STM32/WIZNET hardware verification rather than declaring success from a default build.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted resolution as consolidating STM32 onto lib/wiznet5k and the shared extmod WIZNET driver, allowing the obsolete duplicate driver copy to be removed.
Must explain that changing source paths alone is insufficient: the STM32 integration also needs the current library layout, SPI object compatibility, and pin-interrupt support used by lwIP.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the feature-enabled build results, the PYBV11/W5500 OSError 16 with no SPI transfers, and the lwIP missing-interrupt compile output.
Must not treat a successful default STM32 build as proof of the fix because that build did not enable WIZNET5K.
Must require verification on actual STM32 and WIZNET hardware, including interface activation and network traffic, before treating the consolidation as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technical open-source contributor comfortable editing Makefiles and C integration files and running clean firmware builds, but without STM32 hardware; a second contributor with a PYBV11 and W5500 performs the hardware tests, folded into the simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Collaborative and informal, with frequent progress updates, pasted build output, direct questions, and candid acknowledgment of testing limitations.
